window_selection.criterion: among 10 candidate windows (the 8 best-conditioned windows of the frozen bank-MMSE protocol + the two YS17 windows the task suggested), the one with the highest field correlation under the DEPLOYED path, both at nowcast and averaged over the forecast leads
window_selection.why: AA15a w5 wins on the deployed path (corr 0.636 nowcast / 0.581 lead-mean, the lowest lead-mean nRMSE 0.806) AND is independently the best of all 30 windows in the frozen bank-MMSE real protocol (hand_now 0.461, tmp/wp_real_2026-07-25/wp_real.json) -- two independent criteria agree, so it is not a cherry-pick of the display metric alone.
window_selection.note_YS17: the task suggested YS17; measured, YS17 has NO field skill under the deployed path (w1 corr -0.03, w0 corr +0.01). The YS17 record in memory is good for the ENCOUNTER-point forecast (rho ~0.7, d3_falcon_real_operator) and for the Doppler probe, not for full-field nRMSE.

caveat_two_analytic_arms: The number shown in the GIF (nowcast nRMSE 0.858) is the OPERATIONAL wavesplat/ estimator (SequentialUpdater, v2_konly, N=30). It is NOT the number published for real data: every real-sea result in the program (wp_real.json, the real figures, the blind-auto record) scores the analytic arm with scripts/d3_sa_nomp.mmse_bank_estimate, which gets 0.461 on this same window. The two estimators have never been compared head-to-head on the stereo records; this run is the first such measurement and the gap (0.86 vs 0.46 on the best window) is an open item, not a claim.

YS17_w0.note: Honest contrast: field skill is ~0 at this site; the rho ~ 0.7 on record for YS17 is the ENCOUNTER-POINT forecast, a different metric.

AA15a_w5_bankmmse.note: Research estimator (bank-MMSE) — the arm behind all published real-data numbers. Production-path GIF of the same window: nRMSE 0.86.

AA15a_w5_learned.note: Research LEARNED arm (WavePrior mixed_v1) — behind the published learned real-data number (avg 0.797 vs analytic 0.744). Same window: bank-MMSE 0.46, production path 0.86.
